title: feat: separate community model title from description
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds a nullable `title` column (one-line migration, no curated data).
- Required on create, optional on update; 42-char title, 160-char description.
- Read paths go through `communityEndpointTitle()`, which falls back to
  description → model slug, so `/models` output is unchanged for every existing
  row and nothing has to be backfilled before this ships.
- Shows the title on model cards and in `polli my-models list`.

Replaces the earlier data migration on this branch, which hardcoded 86
`WHERE name = … AND description = …` pairs — a snapshot of D1 on the day it was
written. Rows added before merge would silently get `substr(name, 1, 42)` (the
raw slug), staging/local produce different results, and `name` is not unique
across owners. Backfilling existing titles is a one-time D1 edit, done separately.

Prior work on this branch is preserved at `backup/add-model-modal-ui-elliot`.

Validation:
- `gen` + `enter` typechecks clean
- 44 tests pass (`community-endpoints.test.ts` 28, `tracking-observability.test.ts` 16)
- biome check clean

gist.headline: Models get name tags
gist.blurb: Community models can now carry a proper short title alongside their description. The raw slug may return to its natural habitat: URLs and terminal corners.
gist.summary: Community endpoints now support a required 42-character title on creation and a separate 160-character description, with model cards and `polli my-models list` displaying the title while existing `/models` output safely falls back to description or slug.
gist.impact: Model publishers can give their creations clear, readable names without breaking existing model listings or requiring an immediate backfill of older endpoints.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy community-model garden where each code-plant has a tidy handwritten name tag and a longer description card beneath it. Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses, carefully labels a flowering model plant while a retro terminal shows a friendly `my-models` list; the visual metaphor is giving models human-readable identities while their technical slugs remain quietly useful in the soil.
